_provenance.note: South Dakota citation authorities. South Dakota's operative SNAP policy manual is the DSS SNAP Policy and Procedure Manual, cited by a numbered-section convention such as '9010' (Maximum Allowable Resources) or '13222' (Native American Exemption). This pack defines a single citation family, 'sdsnapmanual', for that numbered convention. South Dakota Codified Law 28-12-3 (the state's statutory drug-felony opt-out) is cited separately as a second family, 'sdcl', matching this roster's Nebraska, Connecticut, Kentucky, Alabama, Louisiana, and New Hampshire packs' multi-family pattern, since this pack expects both citation forms to appear in generated answers.

patterns.note: South Dakota DSS SNAP Policy and Procedure Manual, cited by DSS's own numbered-section convention (e.g. 3920/7370 Convicted Felon Attestation Procedures, 7700 Categorically Eligible Households, 9010 Maximum Allowable Resources, 10110 Standard Deduction, 10210 Medical Deductions, 10300/10310 Shelter Deductions, 10400/10411 Utility Deductions, 11300 Budgeting Income, 13221-13227 ABAWD Non-Work Exemptions). This pack requires the disambiguating 'Section' or '§' prefix in the regex to avoid false-positive matches against ordinary dollar figures and percentages elsewhere in generated answer text, matching this roster's IN PPM/OAC and NH FSM conventions.

South Dakota Codified Laws, cited in the standard chapter-section-subsection numeric format (e.g. 28-12-3, the statutory drug-felony SNAP-ban opt-out this pack cites for South Dakota's full opt-out status).

sdsnapmanual.note: Convicted Felon Attestation Procedures — attestation requirement and process; cross-references § 7370's applicable-convictions list

Convicted Felons — the 2014 Farm Bill's violent/sex-offense disqualification list (aggravated sexual abuse, murder, child sexual exploitation, sexual assault) for convictions after 2/7/2014; NOT a drug-felony provision
Categorically Eligible Households — TANF/Tribal TANF/SSI/Child Care Services recipients only; no BBCE income-ceiling expansion; automatic pass of resource test and gross/net income tests
Maximum Allowable Resources — $4,500 elderly/disabled, $3,000 all other households; categorically eligible households exempt from resource test
Medical Deductions for Persons Over Age 60 or Persons With a Disability — flat $165 standard deduction at $36-$200 in expenses; actual expenses minus $35 disregard above $200
Shelter Deductions — costs in excess of 50% of net income after other deductions; $744 cap for non-elderly/disabled households, uncapped for elderly/disabled households

Allowable Shelter Deductions — rent/mortgage, property tax/insurance, utility allowances, disaster-repair costs, homeless shelter deduction ($200 flat at $199.89-$200 in shelter costs, actual cost above $200)
Determining Utility Costs / Utility Deductions (Allowances) — four-tier SUA/LUA/OUA/PUA structure; body text states SUA $950/LUA $265/OUA $109/PUA $60, contradicting a stale Table of Contents entry
Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) — detailed heating/cooling cost eligibility rules; restates the $950 figure identically to § 10400
Budgeting Income — states the 130% FPG gross / 100% FPG net income eligibility standard directly
Individuals Under Age 18 or Over Age 64 (ABAWD) — current federal ABAWD age scope 18-64
Native American Exemption (ABAWD) — statewide exemption for any Native American individual living anywhere in South Dakota, not restricted to reservation residency; ACCESS code 'I'
Residing With Children Under 14 Years of Age (ABAWD) — exemption applies to all adults in the household, not just the child's parent

sdcl.note: South Dakota's statutory opt-out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban (Pub. L. 104-193 § 115(a)(2)), enacted per a secondary legal-research source (Collateral Consequences Resource Center) dated to 2020; this pack could not independently fetch the statute's text from sdlegislature.gov or Justia (Cloudflare-blocked), see freshness.json
